title: Open PDF as an editable layout (reuse VectorCraft's PDF import)
author: mindmeltde
body:
**Use case**
Agencies regularly inherit print jobs where the client only has a PDF (old flyers, brochures, business cards; the original InDesign files are lost). Today DesignCraft can place a PDF as a graphic (crop boxes, page selection, layers), but not open it as an editable document. That makes DesignCraft a dead end for exactly the jobs where a free InDesign alternative would help most.

**Proposal**
File › Open on a `.pdf` (and `.ai` with PDF compatibility) builds a DesignCraft document:
- one page per PDF page, page size from the TrimBox/CropBox, bleed from the BleedBox
- vector art, images, colour (incl. spot colours and ICC-based spaces) as editable page items
- text as text frames with real characters and fonts
- best-effort reconstruction: lines → paragraphs, column detection → threaded frames, repeated items on every page → parent page, recurring font/size/leading combinations → paragraph/character styles

VectorCraft already reopens PDF and .ai editable (vectorcraft#79, #98: `crates/pdf/src/import*.rs` with text, shading, masks and colour import). Sharing that importer and adding the layout reconstruction on top seems the natural path.

**Out of scope / expectations**
Reconstruction is heuristic, like in Affinity or Scribus. A report (fonts substituted, items rasterised, frames that could not be threaded) after opening would be enough.

Happy to test with real-world agency PDFs (German text, CMYK, spot colours).

title: Placed CMYK TIFF images are exported as RGB
author: japbcoelho
body:
A CMYK TIFF placed in a document is written to the PDF as a DeviceRGB image, in PDF/X-4 exports too, so its ink values are lost: 100% K becomes RGB black and C0 M100 Y100 K0 becomes RGB red. A CMYK JPEG placed beside it keeps its CMYK data.

To reproduce on main `02f187c`, make a 200 × 100 px CMYK TIFF whose left half is 100% K and right half C0 M100 Y100 K0, and the same image as a JPEG, with Pillow:

```python
from PIL import Image
im = Image.new("CMYK", (200, 100), (0, 0, 0, 255))
im.paste((0, 255, 255, 0), (100, 0, 200, 100))
im.save("cmyk.tif", compression="tiff_lzw")
im.save("cmyk.jpg", quality=95)
```

Then place both and export PDF/X-4 with `designcraft-cli script -`:

```
file.new {}
selection.set {"ids": []}
file.place {"path": "cmyk.tif", "x": 72, "y": 72, "width": 200}
selection.set {"ids": []}
file.place {"path": "cmyk.jpg", "x": 72, "y": 250, "width": 200}
file.exportPdf {"path": "out-x4.pdf", "standard": "x4"}
```

In `out-x4.pdf` the TIFF is a `/DeviceRGB`, `/FlateDecode` image whose halves read (0, 0, 0) and (255, 0, 0). The JPEG is `/DeviceCMYK`, `/DCTDecode`, with the original (0, 0, 0, 255) and (0, 255, 255, 0). The export's `warnings` is empty: `check_pdfx4` doesn't look at colour spaces, so it misses DeviceRGB under the CMYK output intent (the page has no DefaultRGB either).

Expected: a CMYK raster keeps its CMYK values in the PDF, as a CMYK JPEG does. Failing that, the PDF/X-4 export should warn about the RGB image.

This matters most for K-only content such as text or line art in a TIFF. After the trip through RGB, conversion to the press profile turns it into four-colour black, which blurs when the plates are slightly out of register.

title: text.select / text.insert offsets (and get_story length) count UTF-8 bytes, not characters; this is not documented
author: htdtkshi
body:
## Summary
`get_story` reports `length: 15` for the 5-character story "はただ商店", and `text.select` anchor/focus values are interpreted as UTF-8 byte offsets. For non-ASCII text (e.g. Japanese) an agent that counts characters selects the wrong range. I could not find the unit stated in docs/mcp.md, docs/agents.md or the command's params description.

## Environment
- Ubuntu (headless), designcraft-cli 0.2.1, `designcraft-cli mcp` over stdio

## Steps to reproduce
In a fresh document (A4), via MCP `tools/call`:
1. `execute frame.create {"rect":[36,36,300,100],"content":"text","text":"はただ商店"}` -> story 9
2. `get_story {"story":9}` -> `"length": 15` (5 characters)
3. `execute text.select {"story":9,"anchor":0,"focus":1}` then `execute text.insert {"text":"Y"}`
4. `get_story {"story":9}`
Reset the text with `set_story_text` and repeat with focus 3 and focus 5.

## Expected
Offsets count characters (as the InDesign model does), or the unit is documented.

## Actual
| select 0..N | resulting text | length |
|---|---|---|
| 0..1 | `Yはただ商店` (nothing replaced) | 16 |
| 0..3 | `Yただ商店` (first character replaced) | 13 |
| 0..5 | `Yただ商店` (first character replaced; 0..5 spans 1.67 chars) | 13 |

So 3 units = 1 Japanese character, i.e. UTF-8 bytes. Offsets that fall inside a character are silently snapped.

## Notes
- n=3 (the table above), plus an earlier independent run with the same behaviour.
- Related but different: #61 (type_text after text.select).

title: [Feature Request] Import QuarkXPress (qxp, qxd) files
author: ewinnington
body:
QuarkXPress has two closely related native formats:

- .qxp — QuarkXPress Project: the modern native document format. It contains the actual page-layout project: pages/spreads, master pages, text boxes and linked text flows, image boxes and references, typography/styles, layers, colors, tables, guides, page geometry, etc. A .qxp can contain one or more layouts.

- .qxd — QuarkXPress Document: the older native QuarkXPress document format, primarily associated with QuarkXPress 3/4-era documents before Quark moved to the project-oriented .qxp format. There are still substantial archives of .qxd files from the 1990s and early 2000s.


For a new professional page-layout/design application, supporting them is strategically more important than their present-day market share might suggest.

The key is legacy corpus, not current Quark usage. QuarkXPress was one of the dominant professional DTP/page-layout systems before Adobe InDesign took over much of the market. Publishers, newspapers, agencies, corporate communications departments, printers and universities accumulated decades of Quark documents.

**InDesign doesn't provide a universal Quark archive importer.** 

-----
Why? My late father left me thousands of qxp / qxd files, including some which have a collection of his dreams, short stories, published manuscripts, letters to my family. Which are now in an unreadable / hard to access format. 

Allowing import of these is a hard reverse engineering problem, but unlocks millions of files across the world.

DesignCraft 0.4.0 on Windows opens briefly/spins and then crashes during startup. Reported on 8 October 2026.

Windows application crash records identify AMD OpenGL module `atio6axx.dll`, exception `0xc0000005` (invalid memory access). Launching the original executable reproduces the crash. Application files were present, the digital signature was valid, and Windows Installer records indicated successful installation configuration. The evidence identifies the crash location, but does not establish whether the underlying defect is solely in the driver or its interaction with DesignCraft.

## Reproduction and workaround
1. Launch the installed DesignCraft executable normally.
2. Observe the brief opening/spinner followed by process termination.
3. Launch with `WGPU_BACKEND=dx12`.
4. DesignCraft opens and remains responsive.

The reporter verified a new DesignCraft window, a loaded DirectX 12 module, no loaded `atio6axx.dll`, and a successful startup log entry. Editing, saving, and exporting were not tested. GPU model, AMD driver version, and Windows build were not supplied.

The first workaround shortcut failed because its PowerShell `-File` path pointed to normal application data while the launcher was saved in Codex's redirected application-data folder. Moving the launcher to Documents / DesignCraft Startup and correcting the shortcut fixed that separate path error. **Summary**: IDML layers come in upside down. body:
**Summary**: In InDesign, a line fits in a text frame when its **baseline** is inside the frame; descenders may hang below the bottom edge. `compose_with_db` requires `baseline + desc <= col.y1`. Tightly fitted InDesign frames (large display type, numbers in badges, two-line headings with explicit leading) therefore go overset on import and the text disappears.

A smaller related issue: `FirstBaseline::CapHeight` uses `asc * 0.72` rather than the font's cap height, which `Glyph::cap` already carries. `XHeight` uses `asc * 0.5` in the same way.

title: [Feature] Optical kerning falls back to metrics, so InDesign-imported text sets wider
author: michaelperna
body:
**Summary**: `KerningMethod="$ID/Optical"` is imported as `Kerning::Optical`, but shaping treats it exactly like `Metrics` (`compose/src/shape.rs`: `if !matches!(p.kerning, Kerning::Metrics | Kerning::Optical)`). InDesign's optical kerning tightens pairs such as `Te`, `“P` and `k”` considerably in display type. Text set with Optical in InDesign is therefore wider in DesignCraft, and tightly fitted frames rewrap and go overset.

**Evidence**: in production signage templates, `Text “Park”` at 68 pt Inter Bold fits on one line of a 367 pt column in InDesign. DesignCraft breaks it after `Text` and pushes the rest of the story into overset. Applying tracking −40 to the same text in DesignCraft makes it fit. This is the main remaining difference after the layer-order and line-fit fixes (#179, #180).

Optical kerning is Adobe's own algorithm, so an exact match may not be possible. An approximation, or at least a preflight warning ("Optical kerning approximated by metrics"), would help imported documents.

title: Fonts activated by font services (Adobe Fonts) aren't found: port VectorCraft #579
author: thaynej
body:
### What happens
On a Mac where Adobe Fonts are active through Creative Cloud, DesignCraft reports them as missing. For example, an IDML set in Minion 3 and Acumin Pro opens with both fonts substituted, even though InDesign, Word and other apps on the same Mac use them.

### Why
`system_font_dirs()` in `crates/fonts/src/fontdb.rs` only scans font folders (on macOS: `/System/Library/Fonts`, `/Library/Fonts`, `~/Library/Fonts`, the MobileAsset font folders and Office's `DFonts`; on Windows: `Fonts` and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Fonts`). Font services such as Adobe Fonts don't install into those folders. They register their fonts with the operating system while they run, which is how other apps see them.

### Suggested fix
VectorCraft just solved this (storytold/vectorcraft#579): it asks the OS for its font list as well as scanning the folders. On Windows it uses DirectWrite's system font collection (5854346, aa5e8f4), and on macOS it uses CoreText's `CTFontManagerCopyAvailableFontURLs` (4b00c2d), reading the files in place. Doing the same in DesignCraft would fix it on both platforms without depending on where any service keeps its files.

This deliberately does **not** scan Creative Cloud's own storage folder. Adobe treats those files as private (an Adobe community manager: "extracting font files from their obscured location is a violation of Adobe's terms of service"), while using activated fonts in third-party desktop apps through the system is the supported route. `file.package` already leaves out fonts whose licence restricts copying, and that should keep covering these.

One design point is yours: VectorCraft's versions use a scoped `#![allow(unsafe_code)]` for the CoreText/DirectWrite calls, and DesignCraft currently forbids `unsafe`.

Related: #48 / #107 (installed fonts in general, fixed in 0.4.0).

In the interest of full disclosure, this was found and analysed with an AI assistant (Claude).

title: Autoflow adds dozens of empty pages when placed text starts with a page break
author: thaynej
body:
### What happens
Placing a .docx whose first paragraph holds only a page break (common in sections split out of a longer Word file) with `autoflow: true` adds far more pages than the text needs. Every page after the first one with text holds only an empty threaded frame.

### Steps to reproduce
A synthetic .docx: a paragraph with only `<w:r><w:br w:type="page"/></w:r>`, then three short paragraphs (`A Short Heading`, `First short paragraph of made-up text.`, `Second short paragraph of made-up text.`), 98 characters in all.

DesignCraft 0.4.0, new Letter document, `file.place {path, page: 1, autoflow: true}`:

| File | `pagesAdded` | Result |
|---|---|---|
| with the leading page break | **33** | page 1 blank (fine: the break asks for that), text on page 2, pages 3–34 hold empty threaded frames |
| same file without the break | 0 | everything on page 1 |

The count grows with the text: a real one-page section of 813 characters gave `pagesAdded: 271`.

**Expected:** 1 page added (page 1 blank, the text on page 2).

### Likely cause
`autoflow()` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/place_text.rs` estimates how many frames it still needs from how much the existing frames show: `per_frame = shown.max(at) / frames`, then `want = (len - at).div_ceil(per_frame)`. A frame that ends at a page break shows almost nothing, so `per_frame` comes out at a few characters. Autoflow then adds roughly one page per few remaining characters in a single batch, and doesn't remove the frames it didn't need. The same overestimate would hit any frame cut short by a break, not only one at the start.

Possible fixes: base the estimate only on frames that ended because they were full, or add pages a few at a time, or drop trailing frames and pages that end up empty once the story fits. I'm happy to try a PR if you have a preferred approach. In the interest of full disclosure, this was found and analysed with an AI assistant (Claude).

title: file.package with idml: the IDML embeds images and links to the build machine's absolute paths, so it doesn't relink elsewhere
author: director-LAC
body:
The IDML that `file.package {idml: true}` writes embeds every image and points each link at an absolute path on the machine that built it. A package built on Linux and opened in InDesign on Windows therefore arrives with all images embedded rather than linked to the package's `Links/` folder.

**Repro** (designcraft-cli 0.5.0, main @ 92649ff)
```
file.new {"width": 612, "height": 792, "pages": 1}
frame.create {"rect": [36, 200, 300, 400], "content": "graphic"}
file.place {"path": "/abs/path/mascot.pdf", "frame": "$1.id", "pdfCrop": "media"}
file.package {"dir": "/abs/path/pkg", "idml": true}
```

| IDML | Size | Image bytes in spread XML | LinkResourceURI |
|---|---|---|---|
| `file.exportIdml` (default) | 15,566 B | yes | `file:/abs/path/mascot.pdf` |
| `file.exportIdml {embedImages: false}` | 9,597 B | no | `file:/abs/path/mascot.pdf` |
| `file.package {idml: true}` | 15,572 B | **yes** | `file:/abs/path/pkg/Links/mascot.pdf` |

`embedImages: false` works on `file.exportIdml`, but the package uses the embedding default even though it has just copied every file into `Links/`.

**Measured in InDesign 21.6 (Windows), IDML built on Linux**
- All 11 placements on one page arrived `LINK_EMBEDDED`.

title: Cut, Duplicate, Paste in Place and pasting text leave an extra undo step that does nothing
author: noah1400
body:
**What happens**
Some commands record two undo steps for one action. The first Undo reverts the action, the second changes nothing, and only the third goes further back.

**Steps** (main a9124a0, headless with `designcraft-cli script`)
```
file.new {"pages": 1}
frame.create {"rect": [36, 36, 136, 136]}
selection.set {"ids": ["$1.id"]}
edit.cut {}
document.history {}
```
`document.history` answers `{"undo": ["Create Frame", "Clear", "Cut"]}`. `edit.undo` answers `Cut` and brings the frame back; a second `edit.undo` answers `Clear` and changes nothing.

The same happens with:
- `edit.duplicate`: `["Move", "Duplicate"]`
- `edit.pasteInPlace`: `["Paste", "Paste in Place"]`
- `edit.paste {"text": "…"}` at an insertion point: `["Type", "Paste"]`

**Expected**
One undo step per action, as `script.run` and tool gestures already give.

**Cause**
`Session::execute_unguarded` (`crates/engine/src/lib.rs`) records an undo entry for every undoable command, also when it runs inside another command (`edit.cut` runs `edit.clear`). `script.run` collapses its steps' entries by hand; other commands don't.

I'm working on this.

**Steps** (main a9124a0, headless with `designcraft-cli script`)

file.new {"pages": 1}
frame.create {"rect": [36, 36, 136, 136]}
frame.create {"rect": [200, 36, 300, 136]}

object.group {"ids": ["$1.id", "$2.id"]}

- `selection.set {"ids": [...], "content": true}` on the two nested objects, then `object.group {}`
- `states.create {"ids": [...]}` with the nested ids (it runs `object.group`)
- a nested object first, plus an object on another spread

**Cause**
`group` collects the named objects that are top-level items of the first object's spread and then indexes the first of them. For nested objects that list is empty.

**Related, not a crash**

title: GREP styles silently ignore invalid patterns (e.g. lookbehind)
author: noah1400
body:
## Problem

A GREP style with a pattern the regex engine can't compile is accepted without any error and then never applies. The user gets no feedback; the style just "doesn't work".

This hits people coming from InDesign: GREP styles there commonly use lookbehind, e.g. for Polish/Czech one-letter words (see #405):

    (?<=\s)[aiouwzAIOUWZ]\s

DesignCraft uses the `regex` crate, which doesn't support lookbehind. The paragraph style is created, the pattern is silently dropped in `crates/compose/src/overlay.rs` (`Regex::new(..).ok()`, and `None` is skipped).

Find/Change already handles this correctly: an invalid GREP there returns `bad GREP: …` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/find.rs`).

## Steps to reproduce

1. `style.character.create` with `{"name": "Sierotki", "chars": {"noBreak": true}}`
2. `style.paragraph.create` with `{"name": "PL", "para": {"grepStyles": [{"style": "Sierotki", "pattern": "(?<=\\s)[aiouwzAIOUWZ]\\s"}]}}`
3. Apply `PL` to a text frame with Polish text in a narrow column

**Expected:** an error saying the pattern is invalid (or the style works).
**Actual:** no error, and the GREP style has no effect. In a headless test at 35 column widths, lines ending with a one-letter word went from 124 of 343 to still 124 of 343. The equivalent pattern without lookbehind, `\b[aiouwzAIOUWZ]\s`, brings that down to 0.

## Proposed fix

- `style.paragraph.create` / `style.paragraph.edit` (and anything else that sets `grepStyles`) reject an invalid pattern with the regex error, as Find/Change does.
- The GREP Style section of Paragraph Style Options shows the error instead of saving the pattern.

- **Lookbehind support** (e.g. via `fancy-regex`) would make more InDesign GREP styles work as-is. It's a separate decision: backtracking runs on every recompose, and patterns from imported files would need a backtrack limit.

InDesign teams collaborate through InCopy's managed files (check-out/check-in of stories with lock files on shared storage) or through Adobe cloud documents. body:
Environment: macOS; DesignCraft v0.4.0-based local build. Not retested on the latest official release.

Documents with **numbered lists that continue across stories** become extremely slow: opening them, every repaint and every keystroke take seconds, and PDF export takes tens of seconds. `Document::list_start` (`crates/doc/src/notes.rs`) orders every story by the page of its first frame to find where a story's numbering starts. For each call it:

3. resolves the paragraph styles of all earlier stories.

`footnote_start` and `endnote_start` / `endnote_order` (`crates/doc/src/endnotes.rs`) follow the same pattern, so documents with many footnotes or endnotes are affected too (`endnote_start` is even called per paragraph during composition).

title: Norwegian hyphenation is one Cargo feature away
author: kapteinmemo
body:
`docs/target-app-parity.md` lists hyphenation patterns for English and Spanish only. `designcraft-compose` already uses `hypher`, and `language_tag` already maps "Norwegian: Bokmål" → `nb`.

Enabling `hypher/norwegian` (covers `no`/`nb`/`nn`) in `crates/compose/Cargo.toml` was enough. Composing a Norwegian test story at `ca343e8` with `compose_story` gave 7 hyphenated lines, all at correct break points: sir-kulasjonen, be-veger, ned-synkningen, kal-ler, over-flaten, bil-de, sjø-fugl.

Happy to open a PR with the feature and a regression test if you'd like it. One open question: the license of the Norwegian pattern source behind hypher's `no.bin` (hypher says it only bundles permissively licensed patterns, but `patterns/` isn't in the published crate, so I haven't checked this one).

title: IDML: custom anchored objects ignore their object style's anchor settings and misplace X
author: aiongg
body:
An anchored object whose `AnchoredObjectSetting` lists only some attributes (for example `AnchoredPosition="Anchored"` with `AnchorXoffset`/`AnchorYoffset`) should take the rest from its object style (`[None]` included): anchor point, reference points, X/Y relative-to. The importer reads only the item's own setting, so the missing attributes fall back to "relative to the anchor, object centre", and the object lands far from where it belongs, often off the page.

The X offset of a custom anchored object also moves the object the wrong way.

Expected: inherited settings apply, and the object sits where the original layout puts it.

title: Section markers show the literal word "Section"
author: aiongg
body:
A section marker character in a text frame (typically a running title on a parent page) shows the word "Section" on every page. The section's marker text (`Section@Marker` in IDML) is imported but never used when text is composed.

Expected: the marker shows the marker text of the section the page belongs to; a section with an empty marker shows nothing. On parent pages the marker shows "Section".

title: Anchored objects with text wrap don't push text away
author: aiongg
body:
An anchored object (inline, above line or custom) with text wrap set doesn't affect the text around it: wrap obstacles are collected only from page items, never from anchored objects, so text runs underneath.

Expected: anchored objects wrap the text of their own story and of other stories, like other objects.

title: IDML: font family names lose trailing spaces; FontStyle "Nothing" is used as a style name
author: aiongg
body:
- `AppliedFont` values are trimmed, so a family whose name ends in a space doesn't match its font.
- `FontStyle="Nothing"` means "no style set here" (inherit), but it is kept as a literal style named "Nothing", so the text falls back to a default face.
